title: Gaplessness indicator by topologically trivial twisting operators
authors: Yuan Yao, Linhao Li, Feng-Feng Song
abstract: We propose several general necessary conditions for quantum many-body system in one dimension respecting U(1) symmetry to be gapped. We show that the ground-state expectation value of topologically trivial twisting operators must approach unity in the thermodynamic limit with a certain finite-size scaling. Equivalently, its violation can indicate gaplessness of U(1)-symmetric Hamiltonians. The topological triviality of such a twisting operator enables us to derive infinitely many other gaplessness indicators by static structure factor to any order in real experiments, which are impossible to obtain by earlier topologically nontrivial twisting operators. We also apply analytic and numerical calculations to test the efficiency and consistency of our results.
summary: This theoretical work establishes a general criterion to distinguish between gapped and gapless quantum many-body systems in 1D with U(1) symmetry. It achieves this by analyzing the finite-size scaling of expectation values involving 'topologically trivial twisting operators.' This provides a robust diagnostic tool, which can also predict measurable decay rates for static structure factors.
main_problem: The authors aim to develop general, necessary conditions for determining if a one-dimensional quantum many-body system with U(1) symmetry is gapped.
main_result: They show that the ground-state expectation value of specific 'topologically trivial twisting operators' must approach unity in the thermodynamic limit for a gapped system. Violation of this scaling indicates gaplessness.
method: The method involves analyzing the behavior of correlation functions and specialized lattice operators (twisting operators) in the ground state sector using techniques involving Fourier decomposition and finite-size scaling arguments.
model_or_system: The theory applies to general one-dimensional quantum many-body systems possessing U(1) symmetry and lattice translation symmetry, including models like spin chains or fermion chains.
key_observables: The primary diagnostic is the ground-state expectation value $\langle 	ext{gs}|U_F|	ext{gs}angle$, which must scale as $1 + O(1/L)$ for gapped systems. Additionally, static structure factors are analyzed.
important_parameters: One dimension (1D), U(1) symmetry, thermodynamic limit ($L 	o \infty$), and the zero average value of the function defining the operator ($ ar{F}=0$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the existence of lattice translation symmetry and assumes certain conditions on the structure factor decay rates for gapped states.
figures_summary: Numerical results confirm that gapped models exhibit $\langle U_F angle = 1 + O(1/L)$, while gapless models violate this scaling. The Fermi sea calculation serves as a concrete example of violation.
paper_structure: The paper develops from proposing initial, restrictive conditions (Theorem 3) to generalizing the diagnostic tool using 'topologically trivial' operators (Theorem 4). It then proves key lemmas regarding operator behavior in gapped systems and derives a general scaling law for static structure factors (Theorem 9).
why_interesting: The development of gaplessness indicators based on local, topologically trivial observables provides a powerful, potentially experimentally accessible diagnostic tool that circumvents the need for complex topological invariants previously required.
